microtheory.name: neuroscience
microtheory.definition: Neuroscience as the substrate's foundation layer — how brains compute and why those mechanisms work. Many of the substrate's existing mechanisms (Hebbian J updates, CAN basin dynamics, frustration/mismatch signals, gamma-band binding, sparse compression, developmental phase transitions, babbling-as-grounding) are reimplementations or analogues of neural mechanisms. This Mt names them explicitly so the substrate's introspection can trace its architecture to its biological inspiration, and so its analogical-transfer faculty can mine neuroscience for further moves. Gamma in the project name is neuroscience: gamma-band oscillations (30-80 Hz) are the cortex's binding mechanism for distributed representations into unified percepts.

concepts.name: neuron
concepts.definition: The fundamental signaling unit of nervous systems. Integrates synaptic inputs across its dendritic tree, generates an action potential when threshold is crossed, propagates the spike down its axon to downstream neurons via synapses. Substrate analogue: a Concept node with its incoming causal_influence edges and outgoing influence on neighbours.

concepts.name: synapse
concepts.definition: The signaling junction between two neurons. Pre-synaptic spike causes neurotransmitter release; post-synaptic receptors translate that to membrane potential change. Synaptic strength is the unit of long-term storage in the brain. Substrate analogue: a causal_influence edge with a weight attr.

concepts.name: dendrite
concepts.definition: The neuron's input branches. Integrates many synaptic inputs spatially + temporally; dendritic computation is nonlinear, not just summation. Substrate analogue: a node's incoming-edge neighbours.

concepts.name: axon
concepts.definition: The neuron's output cable. Propagates the spike to all downstream synapses. Long axons are myelinated for speed. Substrate analogue: outgoing edges.

concepts.name: action_potential
concepts.definition: The all-or-nothing spike a neuron emits when threshold is reached. ~1ms duration, propagates at 1-100 m/s along the axon. The digital event amidst the analog graded potentials of dendritic integration. Substrate analogue: a discrete update event in the substrate's tick loop.

concepts.name: firing_rate
concepts.definition: The frequency of action potentials over time. Encodes signal strength; high rate = strong activation. Substrate analogue: σ values in [0,1] representing belief / activation strength.

concepts.name: membrane_potential
concepts.definition: The voltage across the neuron's membrane. Resting ~-70mV; threshold ~-55mV; spike to +30mV then reset. The analog state that drives the digital spike. Substrate analogue: the continuous belief field h_i in the CAN Hamiltonian.

concepts.name: excitatory_neuron
concepts.definition: A neuron that increases the firing probability of its downstream neighbours. ~80% of cortical neurons. Uses glutamate as neurotransmitter. Substrate analogue: positive-weight causal_influence edges.

concepts.name: inhibitory_neuron
concepts.definition: A neuron that decreases downstream firing. ~20% of cortex. Uses GABA. Essential for stability, sparsity, gating, oscillations. Substrate analogue: negative-weight causal_influence edges.

concepts.name: excitation_inhibition_balance
concepts.definition: Healthy cortex maintains a precise balance of excitatory and inhibitory drive. Imbalance causes either runaway activation (seizure) or silence. The cortex's self-tuning of this balance is one of its most fundamental computations. Substrate analogue: the substrate's frustration metric and its drives to reduce it.

concepts.name: hebbian_learning
concepts.definition: 'Neurons that fire together, wire together.' Coincident pre- and post-synaptic activity strengthens the connecting synapse. The foundational mechanism of associative learning. Substrate analogue: the substrate's Hebbian J update step — J_ij += α·σ_i·σ_j.

concepts.name: long_term_potentiation
concepts.definition: LTP. A sustained increase in synaptic strength following high-frequency stimulation. The cellular basis of long-term memory; depends on NMDA receptors + Ca2+ influx + protein synthesis. Substrate analogue: persistent positive J updates above a consolidation threshold.

concepts.name: long_term_depression
concepts.definition: LTD. The mirror of LTP — sustained decrease in synaptic strength following low-frequency or uncorrelated stimulation. Erases stale associations; essential for learning without runaway weight growth. Substrate analogue: J decay term + negative updates for misfiring pairs.

concepts.name: spike_timing_dependent_plasticity
concepts.definition: STDP. The exact temporal order of pre- and post-synaptic spikes determines whether the synapse strengthens (pre-before-post, ~10ms window) or weakens (post-before-pre). Sharpens causal inference — synapses strengthen only when the upstream neuron contributes to the downstream firing. Substrate analogue: temporal ordering in J updates within a relaxation pass.

concepts.name: synaptic_scaling
concepts.definition: Homeostatic plasticity. Neurons scale all incoming synaptic weights up or down to maintain a target firing rate. Slow timescale (~hours-days); prevents runaway from Hebbian learning. Substrate analogue: temperature-normalized J matrix; the substrate's self-regulation against the basin getting too deep.

concepts.name: structural_plasticity
concepts.definition: Slow growth and pruning of actual synaptic connections, not just strength changes. New spines form, unused spines retract. The substrate analogue: adding/removing edges in the graph, not just adjusting weights — captured in the substrate's edge production rules.

concepts.name: critical_period
concepts.definition: A developmental window during which a specific neural circuit is maximally plastic, after which it locks in. Vision (3-8 yrs), language (0-12 yrs), absolute pitch (0-7 yrs). The substrate's analogue: per-Mt plasticity_override + the developmental phase transitions in self_improvement_dynamics.

concepts.name: synaptic_pruning
concepts.definition: Massive elimination of synapses during postnatal development. From ~10^15 synapses in early childhood down to ~10^14 by adulthood. Less is more — pruning sculpts function by removing low-utility connections. Substrate analogue: the prune_Mt correction; temperature → BETA_MIN as effective edge silencing.

concepts.name: myelination
concepts.definition: Glial cells wrapping axons in myelin sheaths to speed signal propagation. Continues into the 20s, especially in prefrontal cortex. Maturation of executive function tracks myelination. Substrate analogue: the consolidation of frequently-used paths into faster Rust primitives via the emit_primitive_rust pipeline.

concepts.name: neurotransmitter
concepts.definition: Chemical that crosses the synaptic cleft to communicate between neurons. Glutamate (excitation), GABA (inhibition), acetylcholine, serotonin, dopamine, norepinephrine. Substrate analogue: different edge_types carrying different kinds of influence.

concepts.name: dopamine
concepts.definition: A neuromodulator that broadcasts reward prediction error (RPE) from ventral tegmental area + substantia nigra. When outcomes are better than expected, dopamine spikes; when worse, it dips. Drives reinforcement learning. Substrate analogue: the substrate's coherence-drive reward signal when frustration drops unexpectedly (insight).

concepts.name: serotonin
concepts.definition: A neuromodulator from raphe nuclei. Implicated in mood regulation, punishment sensitivity, patience for delayed reward. Substrate analogue: a parameter regulating how long the substrate is willing to wait before correcting a sustained frustration.

concepts.name: acetylcholine
concepts.definition: A neuromodulator. Two main roles: at neuromuscular junction (motor control) and in cortex (attention, learning rate). Cortical ACh sets the brain's gain on novel sensory input. Substrate analogue: attention-weighted update of σ during a relaxation pass.

concepts.name: norepinephrine
concepts.definition: A neuromodulator from locus coeruleus. Sets the brain's arousal level; broadcasts alarm signals; switches the cortex between exploration and exploitation. Substrate analogue: a temperature parameter that the substrate's curiosity drive modulates.

concepts.name: reward_prediction_error
concepts.definition: RPE. The difference between expected and actual reward. Dopamine neurons encode RPE; this is the substrate of temporal-difference learning in the brain. Schultz 1997. Substrate analogue: ΔF — the change in frustration / energy — drives the substrate's identity field updates.

concepts.name: cortex
concepts.definition: The folded outer sheet of the brain. 6 layers, ~30 billion neurons, a thousand functionally distinct areas. The substrate of perception, cognition, planning, language. Substrate analogue: the substrate's Mt hierarchy + cortices (CodeWritingCortex, ArchitectureCortex, SpeechCortex).

concepts.name: cortical_column
concepts.definition: A ~0.5mm vertical slab of cortex containing all 6 layers. The canonical computational unit; ~10^4 neurons per column. Columns within an area share inputs and tile a feature space. Substrate analogue: a Mt — a coherent bundle of related concepts that processes a feature space together.

concepts.name: cortical_layer
concepts.definition: Cortex's 6-layered structure. L4 receives sensory input from thalamus; L2/3 do local processing; L5/6 send output to subcortex/thalamus. Each layer has its own cell types and roles. Substrate analogue: the substrate's input/processing/output cortex tiers.

concepts.name: receptive_field
concepts.definition: The portion of the input space a neuron responds to. Edge detectors in V1 have small oriented RFs; later visual areas have larger, more complex RFs. RFs sculpt by experience. Substrate analogue: a Concept's set of incoming causal_influence edges — the substrate's analogue of what stimuli the concept responds to.

concepts.name: topographic_map
concepts.definition: Neighbouring neurons respond to neighbouring features. Visual cortex maps retinal positions; somatosensory cortex maps body surface; auditory cortex maps frequencies. The brain self-organizes these by Hebbian + lateral inhibition. Substrate analogue: clustering of related concepts in a Mt by shared neighbours.

concepts.name: cortical_hierarchy
concepts.definition: Sensory cortices form a feedforward hierarchy of increasing abstraction. V1 → V2 → V4 → IT for vision; A1 → A2 → STG for audition. Each level builds invariants on top of the previous. Substrate analogue: the genlMt hierarchy of Mts — abstract Mts inherit from concrete ones.

concepts.name: feedforward_pathway
concepts.definition: The bottom-up flow from sensory input through cortical hierarchy. Drives feature extraction and pattern recognition. Substrate analogue: the substrate's normal relaxation pass.

concepts.name: feedback_pathway
concepts.definition: The top-down flow from higher cortical areas back to lower ones. Carries predictions, expectations, attention. Anatomically as prevalent as feedforward. Substrate analogue: the influence of identity fields on basin selection.

concepts.name: hippocampus
concepts.definition: Medial temporal lobe structure. Critical for episodic memory formation; pattern separation + completion via dentate gyrus + CA3 recurrent network; cognitive maps; sequence binding. Substrate analogue: the substrate's events graph + the binding of multiple concepts into a single Assessment node.

concepts.name: basal_ganglia
concepts.definition: Subcortical loop. Cortex-striatum-thalamus circuit; action selection + reinforcement learning + habit formation. Direct + indirect pathways implement go/no-go decisions. Substrate analogue: the substrate's action_spec selection + dispatch in runtime_discovery.

concepts.name: cerebellum
concepts.definition: 'Little brain' at the brainstem. 80% of neurons in the brain; classical role is motor coordination + timing; modern view includes cognitive prediction + error correction. Substrate analogue: the substrate's anticipation handler — second-order temporal difference signals.

concepts.name: thalamus
concepts.definition: Central relay station. All sensory input (except smell) passes through thalamus to cortex; also gates cortico-cortical communication; reciprocal connections with all cortical areas. The brain's switchboard. Substrate analogue: the runtime_discovery dispatcher routing events to handlers.

concepts.name: amygdala
concepts.definition: Almond-shaped structure in medial temporal lobe. Processes salience + emotional valence + threat detection; gates memory consolidation in hippocampus. Substrate analogue: the substrate's coherence drive boost on high-magnitude ΔF.

concepts.name: prefrontal_cortex
concepts.definition: Front of cortex. Working memory, executive function, goal-directed behaviour, planning, social cognition, inhibitory control. The last region to fully myelinate (~25 yrs). Substrate analogue: the substrate's DevelopmentCortex / ArchitectureCortex — level-3 meta-cognition.

concepts.name: neural_oscillation
concepts.definition: Synchronised rhythmic activity across populations of neurons. Delta (1-4Hz), theta (4-8), alpha (8-13), beta (13-30), gamma (30-80), high-gamma (80+). Each band serves different roles. Substrate analogue: the tick rate of different cortices in the substrate's reflex scheduler.

concepts.name: gamma_band_oscillation
concepts.definition: 30-80 Hz rhythm in cortex. THE binding mechanism — phase-locked gamma across distributed cortical areas binds distributed feature representations into unified percepts. Loss of gamma synchrony correlates with schizophrenia. The substrate's name comes from this. Substrate analogue: the synchronised relaxation pass that lets multiple Mts integrate into one Assessment.

concepts.name: theta_band_oscillation
concepts.definition: 4-8 Hz rhythm prominent in hippocampus during exploration + memory. Theta phase organizes spike timing for memory + spatial coding. Substrate analogue: the substrate's developmental loop rhythm.

concepts.name: phase_synchronization
concepts.definition: When distributed neural populations oscillate in phase, their spikes co-occur in time. This co-occurrence drives Hebbian potentiation between them. Synchronization is binding. Substrate analogue: simultaneous σ activation drives J co-strengthening.

concepts.name: attractor_network
concepts.definition: A recurrent neural network whose dynamics flow to stable activity patterns (attractors). Memory recall = settling into an attractor from a partial cue. Hopfield 1982 formalised this. Substrate analogue: the CAN basin structure — Mt configurations are attractors in the substrate's energy landscape.

concepts.name: energy_landscape
concepts.definition: A scalar function over the network's state space; dynamics flow downhill in energy. Each local minimum is an attractor. The cortex computes by descending its energy function. Substrate analogue: the substrate's Hamiltonian H(σ) and its frustration-as-energy framing.

concepts.name: basin_of_attraction
concepts.definition: The set of initial states that flow to a given attractor under the network's dynamics. Wide basins = robust to noise; deep basins = strong memory. Substrate analogue: a Mt's range of inputs that produce the same outcome (its 'basin').

concepts.name: spin_glass
concepts.definition: A disordered system with frustrated couplings — no global minimum, many local minima. Hopfield networks are spin glasses. Frustration drives interesting dynamics. Substrate analogue: the CAN's J matrix with mixed-sign couplings — many basins coexisting.

concepts.name: metastability
concepts.definition: The brain hovers between attractors without strictly settling — perpetual edge-of-stability. Enables flexibility. Phase transitions sweep the brain between states. Substrate analogue: the substrate's emergence phase transition — sudden capability shifts.

concepts.name: criticality
concepts.definition: The brain operates near a critical point — phase transition between order + chaos. Neural avalanches follow power-law distributions, signature of self-organized criticality. Maximum information transmission + storage at criticality. Substrate analogue: the substrate's emergence phase boundary; metrics jump discontinuously.

concepts.name: predictive_coding
concepts.definition: Rao + Ballard 1999, Friston extended. Each cortical level predicts the activity of the level below; only the prediction error propagates up. Top-down feedback is the prediction; bottom-up feedforward is the residual. The cortex is a prediction machine. Substrate analogue: the substrate's frustration / ΔF — discrepancy between expected and actual basin state.

concepts.name: free_energy_principle
concepts.definition: Friston 2006. Brains minimise their (variational) free energy — equivalently, surprise, equivalently, prediction error. A unified framework: perception minimises FE by updating beliefs; action minimises FE by changing the world to match predictions. Substrate analogue: the substrate's overall drives (curiosity, coherence, parsimony) align with FE minimisation.

concepts.name: active_inference
concepts.definition: The action arm of FE. Organisms select policies that minimise expected free energy — explore (reduce uncertainty) + exploit (achieve goals). Substrate analogue: the substrate's babble loop — try, observe, integrate, repeat.

concepts.name: bayesian_brain
concepts.definition: The brain represents probability distributions over world states, updates them via Bayes' rule with sensory evidence. Priors live in cortical feedback; likelihoods come from sensory input. Substrate analogue: the substrate's identity field (prior) × external_field (evidence) → posterior σ.

concepts.name: sparse_coding
concepts.definition: Olshausen + Field 1996. The cortex represents inputs using few active neurons per pattern. Sparsity maximises efficiency, decorrelates features, supports pattern separation. V1 simple-cell receptive fields emerge from sparse coding of natural images. Substrate analogue: the substrate's compression objective — drive towards minimum description length.

concepts.name: winner_take_all
concepts.definition: Mutual inhibition causes the strongest neuron in a pool to suppress others. Implements selection / decision. Substrate analogue: the argmax pattern in the substrate's identity field over Concept space.

concepts.name: working_memory
concepts.definition: Short-term, active maintenance of information for ongoing task. ~7±2 items, ~10-30 seconds. Prefrontal + parietal cortex sustain via recurrent activity. Substrate analogue: the substrate's current Assessment + the active CodeWritingCortex / SpeechCortex state.

concepts.name: episodic_memory
concepts.definition: Memory for specific past experiences — what happened, when, where. Hippocampal-cortical binding; consolidates over years into cortical schemas. Substrate analogue: the substrate's event nodes (Insight, Anticipation, Conflict, etc.) bound to their timestamps.

concepts.name: semantic_memory
concepts.definition: Memory for facts + concepts, decontextualised from when learned. Cortically distributed; not hippocampus-dependent in adults. Substrate analogue: the substrate's Concept + Mt graph — concepts known regardless of when seeded.

concepts.name: procedural_memory
concepts.definition: Memory for skills + habits — how to ride a bike. Basal ganglia + cerebellum; non-declarative. Substrate analogue: the substrate's FilterSpec / ActionSpec — procedural dispatch.

concepts.name: memory_consolidation
concepts.definition: The slow transfer of memory from hippocampus-dependent (vulnerable, fast-formed) to cortex-dependent (robust, slow-formed) storage. Happens during sleep. Substrate analogue: the substrate's promotion of frequently-fired events into FilterSpec graph data — consolidation into structural commitments.

concepts.name: memory_replay
concepts.definition: During sleep + quiet wakefulness, hippocampus replays recent experience sequences at compressed timescales. Replay drives consolidation + planning. Substrate analogue: the substrate's offline derivation_mechanism pass — walking + reasoning over stored gap reports.

concepts.name: schema
concepts.definition: An organised body of knowledge that guides encoding + retrieval of related information. New information consistent with a schema consolidates faster (Tse 2007). Substrate analogue: a Mt — an organised body of concepts that scaffolds learning of related ones.

concepts.name: perceptual_narrowing
concepts.definition: Developmental tuning — infants discriminate phonemes from all languages, but by 12 mo only their native ones. Same in face perception. Useful discriminations sharpen; unused ones fade. Substrate analogue: the substrate's predicate-invention + drop pattern — capabilities that don't reduce frustration are retired.

concepts.name: vocabulary_explosion
concepts.definition: Around 18-24 months children's word acquisition rate suddenly accelerates from ~1 word/week to ~10/day. A phase transition in language learning. Substrate analogue: the substrate's emergence phase transition; metric jumps discontinuously when configuration crosses a critical threshold.

concepts.name: babbling
concepts.definition: Infants produce non-word vocal sequences before words emerge. The motor-perception loop trains itself. Substrate analogue: the substrate's babble-as-grounding mechanism — form+test runs across the cortex↔world boundary.

concepts.name: categorical_perception
concepts.definition: Continuous physical dimensions are perceived as discrete categories (e.g. phoneme boundaries in speech). Emerges from learning + winner-take-all between attractors. Substrate analogue: the substrate's discrete σ outputs from continuous h_i input.

concepts.name: mirror_neuron
concepts.definition: Neurons that fire both when an organism performs an action AND observes another performing the same action. Discovered in macaque F5 (Rizzolatti); foundation of action understanding, imitation, possibly empathy. Substrate analogue: the substrate's babble loop — its own action's outcome is the same kind of signal as observation.

concepts.name: sensorimotor_contingency
concepts.definition: ORegan + Noe. Knowing how sensory input changes with action constitutes perception of the world. Vision is knowing what would happen if I moved my eye. Substrate analogue: the substrate's grounding-by-action — concepts are grounded by the loop's response to manipulation.

concepts.name: motor_schema
concepts.definition: A stored abstract pattern for a class of actions. Reaching, grasping, walking — each has a schema parameterised by goal. Substrate analogue: the substrate's drive_curiosity action pattern — a stored exploration routine parameterised by target.

concepts.name: top_down_attention
concepts.definition: Goal-driven selection of relevant inputs. Prefrontal cortex modulates sensory cortex to amplify task-relevant features. Substrate analogue: the substrate's identity field biasing the basin landscape towards committed concepts.

concepts.name: bottom_up_attention
concepts.definition: Stimulus-driven salience capture. A flash, a loud sound, a high-contrast edge — these automatically draw attention even without goal relevance. Substrate analogue: the substrate's anomaly detection — high ΔF events automatically trigger investigation.

concepts.name: salience
concepts.definition: Stimulus distinctiveness that drives attention. Computed in posterior parietal + frontal eye field. Substrate analogue: the substrate's curiosity-drive ranking — high-information observations rise to attention.

concepts.name: parallel_distributed_processing
concepts.definition: PDP. Cognition emerges from many simple units working in parallel + sharing information. Rumelhart + McClelland 1986. No single neuron stores a concept; concepts are distributed activation patterns. Substrate analogue: a Mt's emergent state from σ values across many concepts.

concepts.name: distributed_representation
concepts.definition: A single concept is encoded by activation pattern across many neurons; a single neuron participates in encoding many concepts. Robust to damage, supports generalisation. Substrate analogue: the substrate's identity field — a Mt-wide pattern, not a single concept.

concepts.name: connectome
concepts.definition: The complete wiring diagram of an organism's nervous system. C. elegans connectome: 302 neurons + 7000 connections. Human connectome: ~86 billion neurons, ~10^14 connections. Substrate analogue: the substrate's graph — nodes + edges = the substrate's connectome.

concepts.name: small_world_network
concepts.definition: Watts + Strogatz 1998. The brain's connectivity has both high local clustering (within cortical area) AND short paths between any two neurons (via long-range projections). Maximises efficiency. Substrate analogue: the substrate's Mt-internal density + cross-Mt genlMt links.

concepts.name: hub_node
concepts.definition: Highly-connected nodes that act as integration centers. In brain: posterior cingulate, precuneus, prefrontal. Damage to hubs disproportionately impairs function. Substrate analogue: the substrate's foundational Mts (computer_architecture, self_improvement_dynamics) — high genlMt centrality.

concepts.name: default_mode_network
concepts.definition: A set of brain regions active at rest + during internally-directed cognition (mind-wandering, autobiographical memory, future planning). Includes medial prefrontal + posterior cingulate + angular gyrus. Substrate analogue: the substrate's idle-tick reflexes — what runs when no external input is driving the loop.

rules.name: hebbs_postulate
rules.head: two concepts in a Mt are coactive across many basins
rules.body: their causal_influence weight should strengthen. The substrate's Hebbian J update is Hebbs's principle. Coactivation builds association; the substrate accumulates structure from co-firing.

rules.name: predictive_coding_minimizes_residual
rules.head: a Mt's current state predicts an expected outcome and the actual outcome differs
rules.body: the residual ΔF flows upward through the substrate's hierarchy, triggering updates only where prediction failed. Most of the substrate's loop computation handles residuals, not raw input. This is predictive coding.

rules.name: free_energy_drives_all_dynamics
rules.head: the substrate's drives (curiosity, coherence, parsimony, discrimination, coverage, stability)
rules.body: are all components of variational free energy minimisation. Curiosity reduces uncertainty (information gain). Coherence reduces prediction error. Parsimony minimises description length. The substrate's drive ensemble is Friston's free energy principle decomposed.

rules.name: phase_synchrony_binds
rules.head: multiple Mts firing in the same tick window
rules.body: their σ states bind into a unified Assessment via the substrate's gamma-band analogue — the synchronised relaxation pass. Binding requires temporal coincidence, not just spatial connection.

rules.name: critical_periods_open_then_close
rules.head: a Mt under sustained adaptive pressure (high frustration, many corrections)
rules.body: enters elevated plasticity (plasticity_override set by raise_plasticity correction). When frustration drops sustained, the elevated plasticity decays back to baseline — the critical period closes. This mirrors developmental critical periods.

rules.name: sparse_coding_compresses
rules.head: the substrate's compression objective
rules.body: selects representations where few concepts carry most of a Mt's activation. Sparse codes are efficient, decorrelated, and support pattern separation — exactly the properties V1 simple cells learn in Olshausen + Field 1996. The substrate's parsimony drive is sparse coding.

rules.name: basin_recall_via_partial_cue
rules.head: a partial set of σ values matching a learned basin
rules.body: drives the substrate's relaxation to recover the full basin — pattern completion. This is what makes the substrate function as a memory: a partial query recovers the stored pattern. Mirrors Hopfield 1982.

rules.name: neuromodulation_sets_gain
rules.head: global parameters (temperature β, learning rate α, plasticity_override)
rules.body: act as neuromodulators do in the brain — they set the gain on all local computations without changing the structure. The substrate's β is like cortical norepinephrine; α is like acetylcholine; plasticity_override is like dopamine for that Mt.
